title: A Wreck for the Monsoon
premise: Jude Underhill, a disgraced railroad engineer hiding in the high passes with a map of lines the company closed and a debt he cannot name, is dragged back into the world when his old rival, surveyor Marguerite Voss, hires his crew to reopen the Kestrel Line before monsoon season seals it. The job is supposed to be simple salvage, but the route crosses a glacier valley where Jude's former mentor died — and where Voss's backers are really hunting a sealed vault of company gold that was buried, deliberately, under tons of ice. As the calving season countdown tightens, Jude must choose between exposing what the company did to bury its crimes and keeping his found family of rail workers alive. In the end, Jude collapses the line behind them, letting the glacier swallow the gold forever, pays his debt with the truth instead of money, and chooses Marguerite and the crew over the career that once ruined him.
about_author: Isandro Ashgrove is the pen name of a former surveyor's assistant who spent six seasons in mountain rail camps before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people whose professions are slowly killing them, and who love them anyway.

chapters.title: The Map of Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Jude Underhill's POV. In a muddy junction town, Jude keeps his crew fed by repairing sidings no one uses, haunted by a debt collector's letter and a compass that belonged to his dead mentor, Elias Wren. When Marguerite Voss walks into the yard offering a contract on the forbidden Kestrel Line, Jude refuses — until she mentions Elias's name. Emotional beat: dread sharpened into reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: Hired Hands and Old Wounds
chapters.summary: Crew POV rotating through Jude's ragtag family: brash young fireman Tamsin, superstitious mechanic Okonkwo, and cook-historian Bramble. They vote to take Voss's contract over Jude's objection, forcing him aboard as their engineer. Voss reveals only part of the plan: clear the line before the glacier calving season opens a two-week window. Emotional beat: found family asserting itself against Jude's instinct to hide.

chapters.title: The Gate at Kestrel Pass
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The expedition reaches the pass where the company dynamited the tunnel shut years ago, officially for 'geological instability.' Jude recognizes the demolition as deliberate, precise, and wrong. First night camp, someone sabotages their water stores. Emotional beat: unease — the past is not just closed, it was guarded.

chapters.title: What the Ice Keeps
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Clearing the tunnel, the crew uncovers a wrecked work train frozen mid-flight, its cargo manifest stamped with the company seal — and crates too heavy for tools. Tamsin finds Elias Wren's field journal wedged in the cab, which she secretly gives to Jude. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into suspicion about what they've been hired to find.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector Rides the Line
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Revealed: Voss's backers are company men who want the buried payroll vault recovered quietly, and her own brother's death on this line is the leverage they hold over her. She confronts Jude privately; he shows her Elias's journal page describing the 'burial order' — the crash was murder. Emotional beat: two rivals recognizing they are both hostages.

chapters.title: Calving Season
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. The glacier begins to groan and shed; the safe window shrinks from weeks to days. The crew pushes the line open through avalanche debris while the company's hired enforcer, Mr. Corliss, arrives 'to assist' — clearly to silence witnesses. Okonkwo quietly arms the crew with knowledge: which bridge timbers will hold, which will not. Emotional beat: solidarity hardening under pressure.

chapters.title: The Burial Order
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Reading Elias's full journal by lamplight, Jude learns his mentor discovered the company crashed its own train to bury evidence of a collapsed tunnel that killed forty navvies — then blamed Elias. The debt collectors have hunted Jude ever since because Elias left him the proof. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose; invisibility was always captivity.

chapters.title: Corliss Takes the Bridge
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. Corliss seizes the half-repaired viaduct and the recovered vault crates, holding the crew at gunpoint as the glacier calves above. Voss plays double agent, feeding Corliss false load calculations. Bramble and Tamsin rig the span's weak timbers per Okonkwo's charts. Emotional beat: terror braided with defiance — the family fights as one.

chapters.title: The Weight of Gold
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, climax. During the crossing, the calving begins; Corliss forces the overloaded vault car onto the rigged span, which collapses exactly as designed, dropping Corliss and the gold into the crevasse. Jude nearly goes with it reaching for Elias's compass, and Voss pulls him back. They run the last train out as the route closes behind them forever. Emotional beat: sacrifice, release, and love confessed in the noise of ice.

chapters.title: A Line That Ends Where It Should
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, resolution. Weeks later, Jude testifies with Elias's journal, burning the debt and the company's cover-up in daylight; Voss turns state's witness against her backers. The crew takes a new contract on an honest coastal branch, with Voss signing on not as a rival but as family. Jude buries the compass at the pass rather than the gold. Emotional beat: peace earned — duty finally aligned with love.
